verdict: The copy is disciplined, specific and unmistakably X-native: every headline is two short beats, the trader examples read like real posts, the claims are honest (design preview, on-device demo, no trial, exact prices) and no banned word or invented proof appears anywhere. It stops just short of best-in-class because one showcase example ends on a line that reads as cut off, and the result captions a visitor sees on their own line slip into shorthand and repetition.
to_95: Replace the Newsletter example so its sharpened line is a finished hook, not 'Why open rates lie:' with a dangling colon (e.g. draft 'So in this issue I wanted to talk about why your open rate is lying to you' -> 'Your open rate is lying to you.').
Rewrite the '1 your call' summary chip into plain English ('1 left to you') and say the your-call instruction once, not three times, in the Try result.
Make 'Why it hits' always state the reader-side benefit; replace the generic '"x" was talk, not the point. The line says the same without it.' used in the final CTA and many live results.
Unify the beat-split wording between the hero ('Split into 2 beats') and the engine ('Split it into two beats'), and de-jargon 'Past fair use: a lighter check, still free.'

issues.where: 'Trades, launches, newsletters.' card, Ana Ruiz row (1440 and 390)
issues.problem: The sharpened output is 'Why open rates lie:' with a trailing colon. Beside three finished lines it reads as truncated, and it is the only proof shown to newsletter writers, the second audience. A colon-ended label is a title, not a hook.
issues.fix: Change the example pair so the result is a complete sentence with a full stop, e.g. draft 'So in this issue I wanted to talk about why your open rate is lying to you' -> 'Your open rate is lying to you.' Verify the engine returns exactly that and that 'Try it' loads the same draft.

issues.where: Try box result summary and helper, on any line with a hedge (e.g. 'i think the fed is honestly going to cut rates in december')
issues.problem: Summary reads 'Cut 1 bit of fluff · Said it plainer · 1 your call', which is not a phrase. The same instruction then appears three times: helper line ('a dotted one to cut it. Your call: i think'), the explainer ('Tap to cut it if you're sure') and inside Why it hits ('Your call: tap "i think" to cut it.'). It is the densest text on the page, shown at the moment the visitor is judging their own line.
issues.fix: Summary chip: '1 left to you'. Keep the single explainer under the editor ('"i think" is your stance on a prediction. Tap it to cut.') and remove the 'Your call: tap ...' sentence from Why it hits and the 'Your call:' label before the chip.

issues.where: Final CTA example and live results where only a filler word is cut
issues.problem: 'Why it hits' is answered with '"literally" was talk, not the point. The line says the same without it.' That explains the cut, not why the line hits, and the same template repeats across many inputs, so the feature feels canned on second try.
issues.fix: For single-filler cuts, name what now leads: '"literally" is gone, so the line lands on 20,000 subscribers.' Use the kept fact or the new first words in the template.

issues.where: Hero result caption vs Try box result caption
issues.problem: Hero says 'Split into 2 beats'; the engine says 'Split it into two beats' for the same move. Elsewhere 'Said it straight' and 'Said it plainer' both appear.
issues.fix: Pick one form per move and use it in both places: 'Split into two beats', 'Said it plainer'.

issues.problem: 'Past fair use: a lighter check, still free.' is internal language; a visitor cannot tell what the limit or the lighter check is, and it sits under the headline promise 'Sharpening is free. Forever.'
issues.fix: 'On very heavy days it switches to the quick check. Still free.'

issues.where: Try box, line starting 'gm. just wanted to say that $SOL at 140 is a gift imo'
issues.problem: Why it hits says 'The run-up is gone, so the first words people read are yours', but the line still opens on 'gm.', and 'are yours' is vague.
issues.fix: When a greeting is kept, name the fact that now follows it: 'The run-up is gone, so $SOL at 140 comes straight after your gm.'

issues.where: Whole page at 390 (header, hero, Try, sticky bar, pricing, final)
issues.problem: 'Start free' is the label in six places including a permanent sticky bar; only the post-result 'Keep it. Start free' and 'Schedule it free' carry the context of the section.
issues.fix: Keep header, hero and sticky as 'Start free'; make the Try-card default button 'Sharpen yours free' is not needed, instead hide the idle 'Start free' under the example result until the visitor has sharpened a line, so the contextual CTA is the one seen there.
